name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network behavior on social media platforms, including the CooRnet/CLSB methodology, its downstream successors, and applications to elections and information operations worldwide.

name: Information Disorder & Disinformation
description: Study of disinformation narratives, fake news, and problematic information circulation across Europe and beyond, including EU-funded monitoring efforts like PROMPT and vera.ai and taxonomies of misleading information.

name: Italian Electoral Media Coverage
description: Longitudinal mapping of Italian news media and social media dynamics around national elections (2018, 2019, 2022), partisan attention, and political parallelism, anchored in the MINE research programme.

name: Platform Data Access & Research Methods
description: Critical and methodological work on researcher access to social media data and APIs in the Digital Services Act era, including consequences of CrowdTangle's shutdown, Meta's URL Shares Dataset, and tool development for platform-independent analysis.

name: LLMs in Computational Content Analysis
description: Integration and validation of large language models for text classification, annotation, and clustering in communication research, including embedding model comparisons and human-machine annotation pipelines.

name: Health Misinformation Networks
description: Cross-national research on coordinated networks circulating problematic health information, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration and studies of health content circulation in India and Nigeria.

name: Political Polarization & Partisanship
description: Analysis of partisan community dynamics, affective engagement, and polarization amplification across traditional and social media, including studies of Bolsonaro-aligned Facebook networks and cross-partisan news interaction.

name: Platform Governance & Content Moderation
description: Examination of platform policy effects on political content visibility and distribution, including Meta's political content reduction policy, algorithmic governance of news feeds, and the shift from open to walled-garden platform ecosystems.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Media
description: Study of generative AI's role in deceptive online content, including synthetic visual persuasion in coordinated gambling promotion and iterative deception strategies in digital information operations, reflected also in current teaching on AI and media.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.
